item.title: Lions create more than $35 million in cap space with restructurings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: One day before their first game of the 2026 regular season, the Lions have cleared a sizable chunk of cap space.
item.content:encoded:
One day before their first game of the 2026 regular season, the Lions have cleared a sizable chunk of cap space.

And all that it implies.

As reported by the folks at Spotrac, the Lions have restructured the contracts previously signed by receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and tackle Penei Sewell.

For Brown, the Lions converted $26 million of base salary into a signing bonus. That creates $20.8 million in cap space.

Sewell's contract had $18.6 million in base salary converted into a signing bonus. The move opens up another $14.8 million in cap space.

Most if not all veteran contracts give the team the ability to restructure the deal, every year. And it's a simple move. The chunk of salary that becomes a signing bonus is then spread over five seasons, with 80 percent of the payment being pushed into future cap years.

With the cap always going up, the move reduces the relative impact of those cap dollars, while giving the team more flexibility in the current year.

For the Lions, that means another $35.8 million in cap space available for 2026. Which officially puts them on the unofficial Maxx Crosby watch list, along with the Cowboys.

Crosby has a $30 million salary in 2026. And the Raiders already tried to trade him once this year, to the Ravens. If the season unfolds for Las Vegas in the same way that most seasons since 2002 have gone (with the exception of 2016 and 2021), the Raiders may decide to try to trade him again — and Crosby may welcome an in-season move to a contender.

item.title: Should NFL mandate early travel for Week 1 international games?
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the conversation continues on the Rams' apparent misfire regarding the decision to barnstorm into and out of Melbourne, there's another question that needs to be asked about Week 1 international games played a long way away from the U.S.
item.content:encoded:
As the conversation continues on the Rams' apparent misfire regarding the decision to barnstorm into and out of Melbourne, there's another question that needs to be asked about Week 1 international games played a long way away from the U.S.

Michael Holley mentioned the concept on Friday's PFT Live. And it's a good idea — the league should treat the Week 1 international game like the Super Bowl and require the teams to arrive early.

If the goal is to export the game to the countries, the effort needs to be more comprehensive. Get there early. Make local appearances. Have multiple press conferences in the place where the game will be played.

It takes the travel strategy out of the teams' hands and makes the issue part of the overall obligation.

Yes, the rest of the story regarding the 49ers-Rams travel adventure will unfold in Week 2, and possibly beyond. But the 49ers seemed to be far more prepared to play given their decision to go to Australia a week early. Having both teams arrive on the same day avoids the possibility that one team will be acclimated and one won't.

Of course, the Rams' experience may be enough to get the selected teams to go early without being told to do so. But why even let it be a variable? The NFL is already imposing on the teams by making them play on the other side of the world. It's not much more of an imposition to mandate the itinerary.

item.title: After arriving in David Montgomery trade, Juice Scruggs is Lions' starting center
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: When the Lions traded running back David Montgomery to the Texans in March, Juice Scruggs was viewed as mostly a throw-in along with the fourth-round pick and seventh-round pick Houston had sent to Detroit.
item.content:encoded:
When the Lions traded running back David Montgomery to the Texans in March, Juice Scruggs was viewed as mostly a throw-in along with the fourth-round pick and seventh-round pick Houston had sent to Detroit. Scruggs was a disappointment as a 2023 second-round pick of the Texans, and he was expected to have to compete just to make the Lions' roster.

Instead, Scruggs will be the Lions' starting center on Sunday against the Saints.

Scruggs was working more at guard than center for most of the offseason, but Cade Mays, who was expected to start at center, injured his wrist a month ago. Mays is now on injured reserve, and Scruggs said he's getting used to his role as the No. 1 center even if it wasn't a role he was expected to play.

"A lot more comfortable, for sure. Things have slowed down. When I got thrown in at center at first it was like, kind of overwhelming, but I'm definitely feeling more comfortable and ready to play for sure," Scruggs said. "You've just got to be ready. You never know when your number is going to get called, so you prepare like a starter, always."

Although Scruggs played mostly guard for the Texans, he did start eight games at center, so he's not new to his position. Even if he's new in Detroit, and playing a part few saw him playing when he arrived in the Montgomery trade.

item.title: Ben Johnson sees Bears practicing at a championship level, unlike last year
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: A year ago, Johnson said his team's practice habits were not yet championship-caliber. He no longer thinks that.
item.content:encoded:
A year ago, Bears coach Ben Johnson didn't think his team was practicing like a team that wants to win the Super Bowl. He no longer thinks that.

Johnson said on Friday that one of his reasons for optimism heading into the season is that he sees better practice habits from his players than he was seeing heading into the 2025 season.

"Here's what I'm excited about: How hard they're working on a regular basis right now," Johnson said. "I think I made a comment last year about how we're not practicing at a championship level yet. I'm not saying that this year. These guys, the work they're putting in throughout the week, it doesn't guarantee you a win on Sunday, but it gives you a darn chance. So I'm happy about what I'm seeing from all of those guys, and as a result from that they all get better."

Johnson's comments about last year's team came after an 0-2 start, when he said, “Our practice habits are yet to reflect a championship-caliber team." After that, the Bears won nine of their next 10 games and ended the season with an 11-6 record and an NFC North title.

This year, Johnson's goals for his team are even higher than just winning the division. He thinks his team is practicing like a team that can go all the way.

item.title: Caleb Williams is one game from tying the franchise record for multiple TD passes
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Bears have still never had a quarterback with 4,000 passing yards in a single season.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears have still never had a quarterback with 4,000 passing yards in a single season. They also have had only one quarterback with multiple passing touchdowns in eight straight games.

By Sunday evening, they could have two.

Via NBC Sports research, Caleb Williams is one game from tying Sid Luckman for the franchise record with eight straight games with two or more touchdown passes.

Williams has accomplished that feat in seven straight games, including the 2025 postseason. It's another example of the team's traditionally anemic offense giving way to an era of significant production on that side of the ball, particularly in the passing game.

Last year, Williams finished the season with 3,942 passing yards. It was enough to break Erik Kramer's 30-year-old record. It seems inevitable that Williams will get to 4,000 yards — possibly as soon as this year.

item.title: Eagles send OC to booth, for first time under Nick Sirianni
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In five years as the Eagles' head coach, Nick Sirianni has had his offensive coordinator on the field with him during the games.
item.content:encoded:
In five years as the Eagles' head coach, Nick Sirianni has had his offensive coordinator on the field with him during the games. For the first time in Sirianni's tenure, the man calling the plays on offense will be upstairs.

"We want to think through every situation to make sure that we're giving ourselves the best opportunity for us to win the game and be at our best," Sirianni told reporters on Friday regarding the decision to have Sean Mannion be in the booth. "Also understanding that there is no right way to do it or wrong way to do it. There's many different ways to do it. I think we can get caught up so much, it's like, 'This is the only way to do it.' You have conviction in what you believe, but there's many different things that can work and have worked. It's just about making the best decision, what's best for your football team and for you to do your job the best. That's how we went about it."

Sirianni was then asked how it will affect him to not have the offensive coordinator by his side during games.

"I don't think at all," Sirianni said. "I mean, obviously, there's communication still, right? We're talking on the headset and everything like that. I would say it's the amount of conversations that happen that have to be face-to-face, I think, are very minimal. I don't think that's -- you're being able to communicate and that's something that we stress on our players of how important communication is. We have to lead that as coaches as well. I don't think that affects us at all."

The balance continues to be seeing the full field for every play and having the ability to talk directly to the players without using a phone. And there is no magic to it. Nevertheless, it will be a different game-day experience for Sirianni, and for players like quarterback Jalen Hurts.

The first test of the new approach comes on Sunday, when the Eagles host the Commanders.

item.title: Baker Mayfield hopes to extend starting record against Joe Burrow to 4-0
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sunday's game between the Buccaneers and Bengals has an intriguing subplot.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday's game between the Buccaneers and Bengals has an intriguing subplot.

Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield has never lost to Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow.

Mayfield is 3-0 against Burrow as a starter. All three matchups happened in 2020 and 2021, when Mayfield played for the Browns.

And, yes, Mayfield faced Burrow in 2022, when Mayfield played for the Panthers. In that game, however, P.J. Walker got the start; Mayfield entered the game after halftime, with the Panthers trailing 35-0.

The Mayfield-Burrow matchup is also one of two Week 1 games featuring a pair of Heisman Trophy winners. The other one happens in Charlotte, between Bears quarterback Caleb Williams and Panthers quarterback Bryce Young.

The Bucs-Bengals game carries greater weight than Mayfield's 3-0 record as a starter against Burrow. Both teams need to get off to a good start if they hope to get back to the playoffs.

item.title: Vikings convert CB Isaiah Rodgers's playing-time incentives into a signing bonus
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers had a solid 2025 season for the Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers had a solid 2025 season for the Vikings. The team has acknowledged it with a tweak to his contract.

Via Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, the Vikings have converted $1.5 million in playing-time incentives for 2026 into a signing bonus.

To earn that payment, he would have been required to participate in at least 85 percent of the defensive snaps in 2026.

Rodgers signed a two-year, $11.045 million deal last year. He's now due to make $5.94 million in 2026.

He can make another $250,000 if he qualifies for the Pro Bowl or $350,000 if he's a second-team All-Pro or, if Rodgers becomes a first-team All-Pro, $500,000.

A sixth-round pick of the Colts in 2020, Rodgers has 77 regular-season appearances with 28 starts. Last year in Minnesota, he appeared in 17 games with 15 starts.

His best game came in Week 3 against the Bengals, when he returned an interception 87 yards for a touchdown and a fumble 66 yards for another touchdown.

item.title: Bills' initial grass field had "major deformations"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In six days, the Bills will host the first regular-season game at their new stadium.
item.content:encoded:
In six days, the Bills will host the first regular-season game at their new stadium. On the second new field there.

The team decided to replace the grass after only two preseason games.

Via Tim Graham of The Athletic, NFL field expert Nick Pappas explained what went wrong with the first field installed there.

"The aspect of the field that appeared to be an issue was that there were major deformations happening, large divoting outside of what we typically see at many of our NFL grass fields — although not something we haven’t seen before," Pappas told Graham. "That lent itself to say there was an opportunity to improve that surface, and that’s what the Bills have stepped up to do and made that decision to replace it."

Pappas explained that, whenever a new stadium is built, "There’s a period before it gets turned over to Bills staff. So, you’re now reliant on the general contractor or the installation company for maintenance over a certain period of time."

He attributed the situation to a "combination of the sod quality from the start, the challenges, and maybe the management up until the Bills’ grounds crew were able to take over, and then you couple it with a very new growing environment that needs to be worked through."

Pappas said the new sod "will come in thicker" than the prior version.

The next challenge becomes preparing the field for three home games in three weeks: Week 2, Week 3, and Week 4.

Pappas thinks another replacement will likely happen during the season.

"Recovery needs to outpace usage," he said. "But if the weather is great and all goes well over that three-game stand, maybe they’re looking at Week 8 to replace it, or they can look at the weather and say, 'Hey, based on where we are today, we have three weeks to recover. We can bring the grow lights out. We can provide our agronomic program with fertility and grow it back.'"

Given the weather challenges in Buffalo, Pappas said he wouldn't be surprised if the Bills need three or four fields per year.

That's one of the reasons why some teams prefer artificial turf. It's cheaper. It doesn't require constant evaluation.

But if teams and owners care about giving their players the surface they prefer, it's worth the money and the effort. Despite the challenges the Bills are facing, they deserve credit for trying to give the players the best possible surface.

item.title: Titans claim G Atonio Mafi off of waivers
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Titans tweaked their offensive line ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans tweaked their offensive line ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

The NFL's daily transaction report for Friday shows that they have claimed guard Atonio Mafi off of waivers. The Raiders dropped Mafi when they claimed guard Bryce Cabeldue on Thursday.

The Titans waived guard Garrett Dellinger to open a roster spot.

Mafi was a Patriots fifth-rounder in 2023 and he played for the Colts in 2024 before landing with the Raiders last season. He started five games as a rookie, but has only played in a reserve role over the last two seasons.

The Titans plan to start Peter Skoronski at left guard and fifth-round pick Fernando Carmona at right guard this week.

item.title: Free agent LB Xavier Thomas suspended three games
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The NFL has suspended free agent linebacker Xavier Thomas for the first three weeks of the season, according to the league's personnel notice.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL has suspended free agent linebacker Xavier Thomas for the first three weeks of the season, according to the league's personnel notice.

It is unclear why the NFL suspended Thomas.

Thomas, 26, was waived from injured reserve by the 49ers on Aug. 26.

He spent time in the offseason with the Texans before reaching an injury settlement with the team May 20. He signed with the 49ers on Aug. 12.

The Cardinals picked Thomas in the fifth round in 2024, and he played 14 games as a rookie and four last season.

He has totaled 10 tackles, 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a pass defensed, all in his rookie season.

item.title: Ashton Jeanty off injury report, set to play Week 1 vs. Dolphins
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Ashton Jeanty is officially "on the mend" no more.
item.content:encoded:
Ashton Jeanty is officially "on the mend" no more.

Jeanty has no game status and is set to play in Las Vegas' season opener against Miami on Sunday.

Jeanty suffered an ankle injury late last month. While the injury initially seemed serious, Jeanty recovered quickly enough to be listed as a full participant for all three practice days this week.

The No. 6 overall pick of last year’s draft, Jeanty rushed for 975 yards with five touchdowns and caught 55 passes for 346 yards with five TDs as a rookie. He is expected to be a significant part of Las Vegas’ offense in 2026 under new head coach Klint Kubiak.

The only other player on Las Vegas’ injury report this week was tight end Brock Bowers, who is out after undergoing a meniscus trim earlier this week. He reportedly will be sidelined for just 1-2 weeks.

item.title: Josh Allen hopes to improve 1-4 career record vs. Texans
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Bills quarterback Josh Allen has a 96-46 record as a starter in regular-season and postseason games.
item.content:encoded:
Bills quarterback Josh Allen has a 96-46 record as a starter in regular-season and postseason games. That's a 67.6-percent success rate.

Against Sunday's opponent, he's right on the Mendoza line.

Allen holds a sluggish 1-4 career record against the Texans, and 0-4 in Houston.

The Week 1 game happens in Houston.

Most recently, Allen was sacked a career-high eight times in a 23-19 Thursday night loss in Houston. He had two interceptions and no touchdown passes in the game.

Countering his one career win against the Texans are eight playoff victories. Per NBC Sports research, that's the most for any quarterback who did not play in a Super Bowl.

As he starts the ninth year of his career, the clock is ticking. The pressure is increasing. While the postseason narrative can't change until January, Allen has a chance to alter his history in Houston by finally getting a win there, in his fifth try.

item.title: Cowboys RB Malik Davis will miss time with a "pretty serious" hip injury
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Cowboys have ruled out running back Malik Davis for Sunday's season opener, and they are bracing for him to miss significant time.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys have ruled out running back Malik Davis for Sunday's season opener, and they are bracing for him to miss significant time.

Executive vice president Stephen Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that Davis was carted off from practice Friday with a "pretty serious" hip injury.

"Unfortunately, I think he's looking at a pretty serious injury that could take him out for some period of time," Jones said, via Nick Eatman of the team website. "We don't have the final details, we'll know more, but certainly so disappointed for Malik. Obviously, tough for our team, but like anything, it's next man up."

Davis won the backup job to Javonte Williams and was expected to play a significant role in the offense. The Cowboys' initial 53-player roster included only those two running backs before they claimed veteran Emari Demercado off waivers as the third back.

Dallas has Israel Abanikanda on the practice squad, and he will likely get a call-up for Sunday's game.

The Cowboys, though, could be in the market for another veteran running back.

Every other player on the roster had full participation Friday, and no one other than Davis has an injury designation.

item.title: Lions release DL Levi Onwuzurike
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Lions dropped a player from their active roster on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions dropped a player from their active roster on Friday.

They announced that they have released defensive lineman Levi Onwuzurike. Onwuzurike would have been guaranteed his entire salary for the season if he was on the roster for Week 1, so a return after the Lions face the Saints could be in the cards.

Onwuzurike was a second-round pick for Detroit in 2021, but he's missed two of the last five seasons with injuries. A back injury kept him out in 2022 and he missed all of last season with a torn ACL.

When healthy, Onwuzurike has 68 tackles, 3.5 sacks and a forced fumble in 42 regular season appearances. He also has five tackles in four playoff games.

The Lions also announced that they have signed defensive lineman Tyre West to their practice squad.

item.title: Ravens rule out LB Teddye Buchanan
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Ravens officially ruled out two players for Sunday's season opener against the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens officially ruled out two players for Sunday's season opener against the Colts.

Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and linebacker Teddye Buchanan will not play. Both are coming off season-ending injuries from 2025.

Madubuike's delayed return was previously reported when coach Jesse Minter gave the team's injury update during his news conference.

Buchanan was limited in practice all week. He tore the ACL and the meniscus in his right knee on Dec. 14 and sprained his LCL in the same knee.

He only returned to the practice field Aug. 17.

Trenton Simpson, listed as a co-starter on the depth chart, will start for Buchanan.

The Ravens, though, have only three healthy linebackers on their 53-player roster, so they are likely to elevate Carl Jones Jr. from the practice squad.

Wide receiver Devontez Walker (groin) is questionable after limited practices this week. Wide receiver Zay Flowers (hamstring) returned to full participation on Thursday and has no injury designation.

The team added defensive lineman Calais Campbell to the injury report as he took a rest day Friday.

item.title: Giants list Malik Nabers as questionable to play Sunday night
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Wide receiver Malik Nabers was a full participant in practice again on Friday, but the team isn't ready to say anything definitive about his status for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Malik Nabers was a full participant in practice again on Friday, but the team isn't ready to say anything definitive about his status for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys.

Nabers has been listed as questionable to play in the team's first game of the regular season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh called Nabers "ready to go" on Wednesday, but Nabers said on Thursday that missing the game is a possibility and that the team is "leaving the decision up" to him.

Nabers tore his ACL late last September and said earlier in the offseason that he doesn't want to return until he feels able to play an entire game without any limitations due to his knee.

The signs from Giants practices of late have been that Nabers is ready for that kind of involvement, but official word isn't going to come until closer to kickoff.

item.title: Klint Kubiak: I was optimistic Brock Bowers would be able to go, but he's not
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: On Wednesday, a curious situation came up with the Raiders, head coach Klint Kubiak, tight end Brock Bowers, and the media.
item.content:encoded:
On Wednesday, a curious situation came up with the Raiders, head coach Klint Kubiak, tight end Brock Bowers, and the media.

During his press conference, Kubiak was asked directly if Bowers and edge rusher Maxx Crosby would be available to play the Dolphins to open the season.

In response, Kubiak said, "We're expecting to have all of our guys ready for Sunday."

But later that day, multiple reporters noted that Bowers will miss 1-2 games after undergoing a meniscus trim procedure on Tuesday. Bowers suffered the injury during training camp, and the surgery to address it was scheduled last week.

“I was optimistic earlier that Brock would be able to go — he’s not,” Kubiak said as part of his opening statement in his Friday press conference. “We’ll get him back soon.”

Given the discrepancy, that did not cut off Kubiak’s questions about Bowers.

“It all happened pretty quick, I don’t remember exactly what day,” Kubiak said on the timeline from finding out about Bowers’ injury to his procedure. “But he got it cleaned up and we’ll get him back soon.”

Kubiak added that he’s not going to talk about a timeline, when asked about the report that Bowers will be out for 1-2 weeks.

“We’ll hope to get him back as soon as possible,” Kubiak said, adding that he was optimistic the tight end would be back this week even after the procedure.

Bowers, the No. 13 overall pick of the 2024 draft, figures to be a significant part of Las Vegas’ offense when he returns. Limited to 12 games due to injury last season, Bowers caught 64 passes for 680 yards with seven touchdowns. As a rookie, he caught 112 passes for 1,194 yards with five TDs.

item.title: Klint Kubiak confirms Fernando Mendoza is the No. 2 QB
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed rookie Fernando Mendoza will serve as the backup to Kirk Cousins.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed rookie Fernando Mendoza will serve as the backup to Kirk Cousins. Kubiak would not previously say whether it would be Mendoza or Aidan O'Connell, but the team's depth chart released earlier this week showed the No. 1 overall pick as the No. 2.

Mendoza is the first quarterback since Baker Mayfield in 2018 not to start Week 1 after being the top overall pick.

"I am encouraging him to know his reads and progressions, to know the game plan," Kubiak said, via Sam Warren of TheAthletic.com. "What the guys take off of each other comes through osmosis. So he's just gotta get his butt ready to roll. The people in front of them are there to produce as well. And if he learned something from their preparation, I think that's a good thing. That's why we have [Cousins] there. But most importantly, we have [Cousins] there to go play and go win the game."

Mendoza won't get many practice reps, but he has to be ready to play as he is one play away.

"That's the life of an NFL backup," Kubiak said. "That's why he's got to be the most mature guy in the room. A guy that can prepare on his own, in the darkness, in the shadows. And then when called upon, go win the game."

Kubiak said Jackson Powers-Johnson will start at right guard ahead of Caleb Rogers, but he considers both players to be starters.

item.title: Chris Johnson unable to travel to Nashville, Titans postpone Ring of Honor ceremony
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Titans' plans to induct Chris Johnson into the Ring of Honor this weekend have been put on hold.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans' plans to induct Chris Johnson into the Ring of Honor this weekend have been put on hold.

The team released a statement on Friday afternoon announcing that they will still celebrate Johnson's career at halftime of the game, but that the official induction ceremony will take place at a later date.

"Due to unforeseen circumstances, Chris Johnson and his family are no longer able to travel to Nashville for this Sunday’s game," the statement said. "Knowing how much he and his family desire to be in person at Nissan Stadium for his induction into the Titans Ring of Honor, we will postpone the official induction ceremony and look forward to celebrating the moment with them at a future date."

Johnson revealed that he has ALS earlier this year. The 2008 first-round pick spent six seasons with the Titans and also played one season for the Jets, who will be the visiting team in Tennessee this weekend.

item.title: Rome Odunze: I feel ready to go; I plan on playing
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze is listed as questionable to play in the season opener because of a calf injury.
item.content:encoded:
Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze is listed as questionable to play in the season opener because of a calf injury. Odunze questions that.

"I feel ready to go," Odunze said, via video from Jason Liser of the Chicago Sun-Times. "I doubt I'm questionable. I know there's a way everybody goes about things, but I feel pretty good. I was out there today. I plan on playing."

Odunze said he strained his right calf, calling it "just a little muscle fatigue" during training camp.

"But, yeah, feel great and ready to go," Odunze said.

He missed five games last season due to a stress fracture in his foot and finished the season with 44 catches for 661 yards and six touchdowns.

"Coming off last year, you hate to have injuries," Odunze said. "Through the offseason, through this training camp, to have been healthy, you can't take those things for granted."

Odunze sounds ready for 2026.

"I can play football, man," he said. "I've been dreaming of doing this since I was 6. Guaranteed opportunity, and I'm trying to make the most of it every single time I step out there. Be excited to go and start a game away."

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Linebacker Jonathan Greenard said on Thursday that he feels "close" to being ready to play after missing all of training camp and the preseason with a pectoral injury, but he's not close enough to be in the lineup this weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Linebacker Jonathan Greenard said on Thursday that he feels "close" to being ready to play after missing all of training camp and the preseason with a pectoral injury, but he's not close enough to be in the lineup this weekend.

Greenard returned to practice this week as a limited participant and the Eagles announced on Friday afternoon that he has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Commanders. If all goes well, Greenard could make his debut for the team against the Titans in Week 2.

Nolan Smith, Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa will be the available outside linebackers for the Eagles.

Second-round pick Eli Stowers is the only other Eagle with an injury designation. The tight end is questionable to play due to a hamstring injury.

item.title: Todd Monken on Deshaun Watson: "I really like where he's at"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: On Sunday, Deshaun Watson will make his first start in almost two years when the Browns take on the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, Deshaun Watson will make his first start in almost two years when the Browns take on the Jaguars.

While Cleveland fans have been clear about their displeasure over Watson still being QB1 in 2026, he will have a chance to perhaps change some minds with his play in Week 1.

After Watson won the QB competition over Shedeur Sanders, he's been taking all of the first-team snaps. That's made a difference in the preparation, according to head coach Todd Monken.

"Watching him get all the reps the last couple of weeks and getting more and more comfortable, how it helped Shedeur in terms of his development by splitting the reps and having a competition, you can see the opposite of that," Monken said in his Friday press conference, via transcript from the team. "He got a lot more of the reps, and you could see him getting more and more comfortable with the concepts, obviously putting the game plan in early and getting him comfortable.

"But I really like where he’s at.”

Watson's task may become a bit more difficult with an offensive line that features rookies at left tackle and right guard.

The Jaguars finished No. 8 in points allowed and No. 11 in yards allowed last season.

item.title: Bears, D'Andre Swift agree to three-year contract extension
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bears running back D'Andre Swift will kick off the new season with a new contract.
item.content:encoded:
Bears running back D'Andre Swift will kick off the new season with a new contract.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Swift has agreed to a three-year contract extension in Chicago. The deal is worth $33.75 million and includes $27.5 million in guaranteed money.

Swift's new deal comes after Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson, and Jonathan Taylor agreed to new deals over the summer.

Swift joined the Bears in 2024 and has started 33 regular season games since coming to Chicago. He had 476 carries for 2,046 yards and 15 touchdowns while also catching 76 passes in those appearances. He added 32 carries for 130 yards and a touchdown in the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Texans second-round pick Kayden McDonald won't be making his NFL debut in September.

The team announced that McDonald has been placed on injured reserve on Friday. McDonald missed the last two days of practice with an ankle injury.

With McDonald out of commission for four games, the Texans moved to bolster their defensive line options. They announced that they have signed Jaden Crumedy to the 53-man roster.

Crumedy was in training camp with the Packers, but did not make it through their final cuts. He had 15 tackles and a half-sack in eight games for the Panthers over the last two seasons.

item.title: Shemar Stewart doubtful, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins set to play Week 1
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Bengals are unlikely to have defensive end Shemar Stewart for Sunday's season opener against the Buccaneers, but the rest of their 53-man roster is healthy to play — including receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals are unlikely to have defensive end Shemar Stewart for Sunday's season opener against the Buccaneers, but the rest of their 53-man roster is healthy to play — including receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

Cincinnati has listed Stewart (knee) as doubtful for the contest.

Stewart was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, but was downgraded to limited on Thursday. He was downgraded once again on Friday as he did not participate in the day's session.

In eight games as a rookie last season, Stewart recorded 11 total tackles with one sack, two tackles for loss, and four quarterback hits.

As has been the expectation all week, Chase (knee) and Higgins (foot) are set to play. Chase did not practice Friday, but it was considered a rest day.

Cornerback DJ Turner (hamstring) is also set to play despite being limited in practice over the last two days.

Kickoff for Sunday’s matchup between the Bengals and Bucs is set for 1 p.m. ET.

item.title: RB Malik Davis carted off at Cowboys practice
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys may need to pivot to a new plan for their offensive backfield ahead of Sunday night's game against the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys may need to pivot to a new plan for their offensive backfield ahead of Sunday night's game against the Giants.

According to multiple reports, running back Malik Davis had to be carted off the field at Friday's practice after suffering an injury. There's been no word from the team about Davis's condition yet, but the team will issue their final injury report of the week later in the day.

Davis is listed as the No. 2 running back behind Javonte Williams. Emari Demercado, who was claimed off of waivers on August 31, is the other back on the 53-man roster.

The Cowboys also have Israel Abanikanda on the practice squad and an evaluation of Davis's condition will likely determine if he'll be called up for the opener.

item.title: Packers release Bo Melton, but will bring him back on practice squad
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Packers have made a surprising roster move on Friday, but there’s more to it than it initially appears.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers have made a surprising roster move on Friday, but there’s more to it than it initially appears.

Green Bay has released receiver Bo Melton, but there’s more to it than it appears.

According to multiple reporters on the Packers beat, this is a roster management move, as Melton is expected to re-sign with the club’s practice squad and get elevated to the gameday roster for the Week 1 matchup against the Vikings.

Melton, a seventh-round pick in 2022, is now a vested veteran, which means he does not need to clear waivers to go to the practice squad.

In 16 games last season, Melton caught four passes for 107 yards with a touchdown. He also took five carries for 35 yards. He was on the field for 47 percent of special teams snaps and 10 percent of offensive snaps in games played.
